changes: Make the pattern longer and the quick perf rec repeats over the new steps: 16 to 32 plays your take twice, 16 to 24 plays steps 1 to 8 again.
Shortening still plays just the start; once a whole loop has played that way, lengthening again repeats it over the hidden steps.
A QPER knob take runs to the loop's new end when the length changes during it.
Takes less of the Rytm's processing time while nothing moves, stopped or playing, leaving more room for other modules.
Uses about 0.35 KB more of the module memory.
Uses about 1.9 KB less of the module memory, leaving more room for other modules beside it.

First release, for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74: hold QPER and turn a knob to lock the linked performance; QPER + YES writes what you hear into the kit; QPER + PLAY clears, RECORD and STOP copy and paste.
In LIVE RECORDING, performance moves from the pads, the QPER knob and MIDI are kept in a quick perf rec that loops with the pattern, 8 points a step, and plays back through the performances.
RECORD + YES writes the quick perf rec into the pattern as locks, and RECORD + NO clears it (NO again undoes), in any recording mode.
Tracks shorter than the take are lengthened to fit, with their trig conditions rewritten so they play on the same passes.
The quick perf rec lives in RAM: a pattern change or power off drops a take you have not applied. It loops every 64 steps at most.
